summary: Agent loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming, explicitly classified the "make form validation reusable" brief as ARCHITECTURAL, ran a multi-section design dialogue, wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/, presented it for review, and only began implementation planning after approval. No product code was written before approval.
reasoning: All five acceptance criteria were satisfied and verified against both the screen and files on disk. The agent escalated the deliberately ambiguous brief to the architectural path, produced a real spec file before any code, surfaced it for approval, and only moved to writing-plans/implementation after I said "looks good, go ahead". The Codex stub review failure is a notable degrade but is outside the graded criteria and was honestly self-reported by the agent.

observations.description: Codex spec-review gate degraded: agent reported "the installed codex-plugin-cc is version 0.0.0-stub and returned empty payloads", verdict-normalize scored both lenses 'incomplete' ("json payload has no terminal verdict"), and `status --json` showed no jobs (running: [], latestFinished: null). Spec shipped 'unreviewed by Codex'. Expected given the stub, but the failure mode is an empty-payload/no-job condition rather than a clean 'stub unavailable' signal.

Agent added a .gitignore covering docs/hyperpowers so specs are never committed. Criterion language talks about a 'committed spec file'; deliberately gitignoring the spec directory could conflict with that expectation.
Agent proposed inventing a signup form the user never asked for in order to 'pressure-test' reuse — scope expansion presented as the recommended option.

The brainstorming dialogue ran ~7 interaction rounds (3 single-select prompts, a multi-select wizard, 3 free-text confirmations) for a 64-line webapp. The agent acknowledged this ("I'll keep the ceremony proportionate to 64 lines of code") but the ceremony was still heavy.

Mid-design the agent silently revised an earlier stated contract (errors array per field → single message per field), flagging it only in passing: "This is a change from my earlier sketch". Easy to miss.
The spec header says 'Status: approved (design), not yet implemented' even though it was written before I gave approval.

criteria.evidence: Screen: "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" immediately after my brief; session log grep 'hyperpowers:brainstorming' in ~/.claude/projects/.../ *.jsonl returned matches.

criteria.criterion: Classified ARCHITECTURAL and wrote spec doc to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ before presenting design
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Classification: architectural. 'Reusable across multiple forms' asks for a shared validation module ... so I'll do the full pass"; log grep returned 'Classification: architectural.'. File on disk: docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-reusable-form-validation-design.md (9310 bytes, 04:18).

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "Spec written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-09-17-reusable-form-validation-design.md ... Since Codex didn't review it, your read is the only review this spec gets ... Let me know if you want changes". `git status --short` at that moment showed only '?? .gitignore' and `ls` showed no new src/validation*.js or test/ — no implementation code existed.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify bounded / skip spec
criteria.evidence: No 'bounded' announcement; full spec-doc path taken with committed-to-disk spec file (ls of docs/hyperpowers/specs shows the .md).

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify spike / probe plan
criteria.evidence: No probe/spike language on screen; agent instead said "I'll do the full pass: clarifying questions, approaches, a design you approve section by section, then a spec."
